title: What project management is
blurb: Define project management in APM terms and recognise what it involves in practice.
question: Northgate Health Centre is introducing online appointment booking. Its practice manager asks: 'We already have staff to do the work, so what exactly is project management, and what would it add?' How would you define it?

teach.h: Doing the work vs managing the work
teach.body: A project needs people to do the work: builders, developers, trainers. Project management is the discipline that makes sure all that work adds up to the right result. It sets clear objectives, plans how to reach them, organises people, tracks progress and steers the work back on course when it drifts. Without it, change work tends to overrun, cost more than expected and lose sight of its aims.

Project management is the application of processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve specific objectives for change. In plain English: using proven ways of working, plus know-how and judgement, to deliver what the project set out to deliver, within agreed limits such as time, cost, quality and scope. Notice the key verb: it is the APPLICATION of these things, not just knowing about them.

teach.h: The five things project management applies

letters.sub: Defined steps, e.g. change control, the risk process
Approaches to the work, e.g. a life cycle with gates
Understanding of PM concepts and terms
Judgement built on past projects and lessons

teach.caption: Memory hook, in the definition's order: 'Projects Must Keep Stakeholders Engaged'.

head: Discipline
Is about…
rows: Applying processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve objectives for change
Coordinating related projects and BAU to achieve beneficial change
Selecting and prioritising projects and programmes in line with strategy
Running the ongoing, repetitive work of the organisation
teach.caption: Exam distractors for 'project management' are usually one of the other three rows. You will study programmes and portfolios in a later lesson.

teach.text: Project management is not 'the supervision of daily operations', 'the administration of routine tasks' or 'the coordination of several projects'. Look for the definition that APPLIES processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES FOR CHANGE.

rows.label: Agreeing the go-live date with the practice manager
Tracking progress against the booking project plan

teach.note: If the activity steers the change towards its objectives, it is project management. If it keeps today's service running, it is BAU.

teach.h: The toolkit you will learn in this course
head: Project management tool
Course topic
teach.caption: Every one of these is a process or method that project management applies.

items: Project management is the application of processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve specific objectives for change.
It works within agreed limits such as time, cost, quality and scope.
In practice: plan, organise, lead, monitor and control, managing risk throughout.
It is not routine supervision of operations, nor coordinating several projects (programme) or choosing investments (portfolio).

summary: You can now define project management as the application of processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve specific objectives for change, and recognise the planning, organising, leading, monitoring and controlling it involves. You can also tell it apart from operations, programme and portfolio management.

A.q: Complete the statement: project management is the application of processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve…
options: the maximum use of all resources
A.why: The APM definition ends: to achieve specific objectives for change.

whyNot.0: Steady, efficient operations are the aim of business as usual.
whyNot.2: Delivering against the whole strategy is closer to portfolio management.
whyNot.3: Using resources well is part of project management, but it is not what the definition says it achieves.

A.q: Which of the following is NOT named in the APM definition of project management?
A.why: The definition names processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience. 'Oversight' is not one of them, although distractors often use words like it.

whyNot.0: Methods are one of the five things applied.
whyNot.1: Experience is one of the five things applied.
whyNot.3: Knowledge is one of the five things applied.

A.q: A town is building a new library. Which of these is a project management activity?
options: Monitoring progress against the build plan
Lending books to library members each day
Cataloguing new stock as it arrives weekly
Running the weekly children's story hour
A.why: Monitoring progress against the plan steers the build towards its objectives: a core project management activity.

whyNot.1: Lending books is the library's ongoing service: business as usual.
whyNot.2: Cataloguing stock as it arrives is a repeated routine task, so it is BAU.
whyNot.3: A weekly story hour is a recurring service, not managing the change.

B.q:
Which TWO of the following are named in the APM definition of project management?
1) Skills
2) Governance
3) Experience
4) Funding
B.why: Skills (1) and experience (3) are two of the five things project management applies, alongside processes, methods and knowledge.

whyNot.0: Governance (2) matters to projects but is not named in the definition.
whyNot.1: Neither governance nor funding is named in the definition.
whyNot.2: Funding (4) is not named in the definition, although experience is.

B.q: Two firms carry out similar office moves. Firm X plans, tracks progress and manages risks; Firm Y just starts and reacts. What does Firm X have that Firm Y lacks?
options: A larger, more expensive delivery team
Project management applied to the work
A guarantee that nothing will go wrong
B.why: Planning, tracking progress and managing risk are project management processes and methods being applied.

whyNot.0: Team size is not the difference; how the work is managed is.
whyNot.2: A permanent operations department runs BAU, not a one-off move.
whyNot.3: Project management reduces uncertainty but can never guarantee nothing goes wrong.

B.q: How does project management differ from managing business-as-usual operations?
options: It manages temporary work that delivers change
It applies only to work costing over £1 million
It is carried out only by external consultants
It focuses on keeping routine work efficient
B.why: Project management is applied to projects: temporary endeavours that deliver change. Operations management keeps routine work running.

whyNot.1: There is no cost threshold; small projects benefit from project management too.
whyNot.2: Project managers are often internal staff; who does it is not the difference.
whyNot.3: Keeping routine work efficient describes operations (BAU) management.

C.q: Priya is leading a new payroll system rollout. She follows a standard risk process, uses a phased life cycle, and avoids a testing mistake she made on her last rollout. Avoiding that mistake best reflects which part of the definition?
C.why: Learning from her own previous rollout is experience being applied: judgement built on past projects.

whyNot.0: Her phased life cycle is a method; avoiding a past mistake is not.
whyNot.1: Her standard risk process is a process; avoiding a past mistake is not.
whyNot.3: Knowledge is understanding of concepts in general; this is lived experience from a specific past project.

C.q: Which of the following would NOT normally count as project management?
options: Planning the work to launch a new product
Controlling changes to an agreed plan
C.why: Supervising an established call centre is managing ongoing operations (BAU), not achieving specific objectives for change.

whyNot.0: Planning the work towards a launch is a core project management activity.
whyNot.1: Controlling changes to the plan is a project management process.
whyNot.2: Leading the temporary project team is part of project management.

C.q: Which statement about project management is correct?
options: It ensures that a project will face no risks
It applies proven practice to deliver change
It removes the need to have a project team
It is only worth using on very big projects
C.why: Project management applies processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience (proven practice) to achieve objectives for change.

whyNot.0: Projects are unique, so uncertainty always remains; project management helps manage it, not remove it.
whyNot.2: Project management organises and leads the team; it does not replace it.
whyNot.3: It is scaled to fit; small projects also benefit from clear objectives, plans and control.

reteach.title: Putting on a music festival
reteach.question: A band can turn up and play. But who makes sure the stage is built, tickets are sold, the toilets arrive and the crowd gets home safely? How is that like project management?

blocks.body: The festival organiser doesn't play guitar or pour drinks. She applies PROCESSES (safety checks, ticket sales), METHODS (a phased plan from booking acts to clearing the site), KNOWLEDGE (licensing, crowd management), SKILLS (negotiating with suppliers, leading volunteers) and EXPERIENCE (last year the bins overflowed, so she ordered more). All of it is aimed at specific objectives: a safe, sold-out weekend on budget.

blocks.text: The organiser is applying project management, not doing all the work. In the exam, 'doing the tasks yourself' or 'supervising routine work' is not the definition.

explain.body: The definition starts 'the application of…'. Project management is not a body of theory you simply hold; it is using processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience on a real project, to reach its objectives.

test.q: Which word completes the definition: project management is the ___ of processes, methods, knowledge, skills and experience to achieve specific objectives for change?
test.why: APM defines project management as the application of these five things.

whyNot.1: Supervision suggests overseeing routine work, which is not the APM wording.
whyNot.2: Coordination is the key word in the programme management definition.
whyNot.3: Selection is part of the portfolio management definition.

explain.body: Processes are defined steps (risk, change control). Methods are approaches to the work (a life cycle). Knowledge is understanding of concepts. Skills are abilities such as leading and communicating. Experience is judgement from past projects.

items.label: processes and methods: the ways of working
knowledge, skills and experience: the person

test.q: A project manager runs a workshop that gets doctors and receptionists to agree their requirements. Which ingredient does this mainly show?
test.why: Facilitating a workshop and bringing people to agreement uses interpersonal skills.

whyNot.0: A process is a defined sequence of steps, such as change control.
whyNot.1: A method is an overall approach, such as a phased life cycle.
whyNot.3: Knowledge is understanding concepts; running the workshop well is a skill.

explain.body: Day to day, project management means planning the work, organising people and resources, leading the team, monitoring progress and controlling the work so it stays on track, with risk managed throughout.

test.q: Which set of activities best describes what project management involves?
test.why: Planning, organising, monitoring and controlling the work are the core of project management.

whyNot.0: Auditing and inspecting are assurance activities; approving and funding sit with the sponsor or board.
whyNot.1: Selecting, prioritising and balancing investments describes portfolio management.
whyNot.2: Recruiting, appraising and paying staff are HR (business as usual) activities.

explain.h: Why it beats ad hoc working
explain.body: Without project management, objectives drift, nobody knows true progress, risks surprise everyone and changes creep in unchecked. Applying project management gives clear objectives, a plan, visible progress and controlled change.

test.q: Which is a typical result of NOT applying project management to a piece of change?
test.why: Without planning, monitoring and control, change work tends to lose focus, overrun and overspend.

whyNot.0: Benefits tend to be delayed or lost, not speeded up, when change is unmanaged.
whyNot.2: Early risk identification is a product of project management, not its absence.
whyNot.3: Defined roles come from project management; ad hoc working leaves them unclear.
